subject: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace route for Redwood evaluation (CloudBridge)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dana White <dana.white@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace route for Redwood evaluation (CloudBridge)

Hi Dana — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and a few questions so we can align the commercial path: 

- What we heard: CloudBridge is evaluating Redwood for chat and embedding inference for your internal agent and customer portal (high throughput, spikes during EMEA hours).
- Procurement posture we heard on the call: preference to keep purchase on corporate card if possible for quick pilots, but procurement may require a PO for production/enterprise.
- Marketplace interest: you mentioned AWS Marketplace could simplify procurement for your finance team.

To move this forward, can you confirm: 
1) Do you have a named procurement contact (email) we should loop in for a PO path?
2) Is AWS Marketplace the preferred route if we can list under our marketplace offering, or would you prefer a direct PO/Invoice route?
3) Any specific legal/compliance gating items your procurement team requires (e.g., vendor questionnaire, SOC evidence, reseller master agreement)?

I've attached a short marketplace vs PO checklist to illustrate the steps and typical timelines for both routes (attachment: redwood-enterprise-marketplace-checklist.pdf). If you'd like, Karthik from our Billing & GTM ops can join the procurement intro to outline tradeoffs and timing.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm procurement contact + preference (card vs PO vs marketplace)
- If PO, provide vendor name & billing address so we can prepare SOW/pricing and an initial PO template
- If marketplace, we can share listing requirements and an estimated time-to-list to match your procurement timeline

Thanks — I can be flexible on time for a short follow-up with procurement (15–20m).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-enterprise-marketplace-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Dana White <dana.white@cloudbridge.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.io>, Alicia Park <alicia.park@cloudbridge.io>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 17:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace route for Redwood evaluation (CloudBridge)

Hi Hannah — thanks for the summary. Good recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Procurement contact: procurement@cloudbridge.io. Alicia Park (cc'd) is the procurement lead; she handles PO processes and vendor onboarding.
2) Preference: for pilot we'd prefer payment by card to move faster, but procurement will require a PO and standard vendor onboarding for anything beyond pilot.
3) Legal: Procurement requests an initial vendor form, vendor MTU, and SOC 2 report (or attestation). They will also need an example SOW and pricing breakdown to approve budget.

AWS Marketplace is attractive because it reduces the number of internal approvals for subscriptions, but procurement tends to prefer PO for contract visibility and internal cost allocation. If the AWS Marketplace listing can be invoiced to our corporate account with a PO, that's ideal.

Our target for a pilot start is the week of 7/19. If you can share a draft SOW and ballpark pricing today or tomorrow, we can route internally.

Thanks,
Dana
Director of Product Operations | CloudBridge
dana.white@cloudbridge.io
[Sent from mobile]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 20:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: procurement options — quick notes

Hannah / Marissa — following Dana's replies, a couple of quick operational notes we should surface to procurement: 

- AWS Marketplace path: Pros = faster approval cycles for some customers, consolidated billing through AWS, good for subscriptions. Cons = requires marketplace listing prep (payee details, pricing bands, AWS listing timeframe ~2–3 weeks), and some enterprises still ask for PO/AP overlay.
- PO/direct invoice path: Pros = straightforward for procurement, supports one-off SOWs/consumable billing. Cons = slower for pilot if finance needs new vendor onboarding (can be 7–14 business days).

Action items for us to prepare ASAP: 
1) Draft SOW (we have a short template) + ballpark pricing tiers (attached sample pricing estimate).
2) Vendor onboarding packet & SOC 2 attestation link.
3) If they prefer marketplace, we need the AWS billing entity (company tax name + address) and the HubSpot company record is helpful for our Marketplace ops team.

Hannah — I'll drop the pricing estimate and SOW template into the thread; feel free to send to procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
[karthik note: will follow up with marketplace checklist link]
[Attachment: pricing-estimate-cloudbridge.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Hi Alicia / procurement team — thanks for being looped in. Per Dana and Karthik, attaching a short SOW template and a ballpark pricing sheet for the pilot (30-day, up to 50K tokens/day with autoscaling spikes).

What we need from you to proceed with a PO or marketplace listing: 
- Official vendor name to appear on PO (legal entity)
- Billing address & tax ID (for PO and/or marketplace registration)
- Preferred payment route: PO to vendor (invoice) OR purchase via AWS Marketplace (if so, please confirm the Marketplace billing account ID or buyer organization id)
- Any specific vendor form or W9 we should complete — we've attached our standard vendor packet and SOC 2 access link in the shared doc.

Attachments: redwood-sample-sow.docx, pricing-estimate-cloudbridge.xlsx, redwood-enterprise-marketplace-checklist.pdf

Proposed next steps: 
- If you confirm vendor name + billing details today, we can generate a draft SOW and an initial invoice/PO template for your review by EOD.
- If you prefer Marketplace, we can begin listing prep in parallel and share expected listing timeline (typically 10–14 business days once all listing info is provided).

Would you be available for a short 20 minute call this Thursday (7/8) to finalize the route?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
